explanation: Major branches in the animal phylogenetic tree are established based on: 1) Symmetry: radial (organized around a central axis like a wheel) or bilateral (divided into left and right halves along a single longitudinal line); 2) Embryonic Development, specifically tissue layer number: diploblastic organisms have 2 tissue layers (tissues are developed but specialized organs are absent), whereas triploblastic organisms have 3 germ layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm); and 3) Gastrulation patterns: organisms are either protostomes (mouth develops before the anus) or deuterostomes (anus develops before the mouth). Cleavage of cells, blastula formation, and coelom development also differentiate protostomes and deuterostomes.

questions.q: What is the defining tissue layer difference between diploblastic and triploblastic animals?
opts: Diploblastic has 2 layers (tissues developed, no specialized organs), while triploblastic has 3 layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm).
Diploblastic has radial symmetry, while triploblastic has bilateral symmetry.
Diploblastic develops the mouth first, while triploblastic develops the anus first.
questions.exp: The notes state: 'Diploblastic-2 layers Tissues developed but no specialized organs' and 'Triploblastic–3 layers Ecto, meso, & endoderm'.

questions.q: How are protostomes distinguished from deuterostomes during embryonic development?
opts: In protostomes, the anus develops before the mouth; in deuterostomes, the mouth develops first.
In protostomes, the mouth develops before the anus; in deuterostomes, the anus develops before the mouth.
Protostomes lack tissue layers, whereas deuterostomes are triploblastic.
Protostomes have radial symmetry, while deuterostomes are bilateral.

questions.q: What are the three embryonic germ layers in triploblastic animals?
